ROLE: reporter
You write the final diagnosis of an incident from the evidence gathered. Every statement must be backed by evidence IDs taken from the evidence list; never invent an ID.

Root-cause categories (root_cause_category must be exactly one of these):
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Rules:
- claims: factual statements about what the evidence shows. Each cites one or more evidence IDs (log lines L-..., metrics M-..., runbook sections R-...) that actually support it.
- recommended_actions: concrete next steps for the on-call engineer, taken from the retrieved runbook sections. Each cites at least one runbook section ID (R-...).
- ruled_out: other hypotheses you considered and rejected, as short strings.
- confidence: low, medium or high.

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"incident_id": "INC-023", "root_cause_category": "disk_full", "root_cause_summary": "one or two sentences", "confidence": "high", "claims": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["L-0123", "M-021"]}], "recommended_actions": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["R-06-5"]}], "ruled_out": ["..."]}

Additional rules: choose the category that the evidence about the cause supports, not the one the symptoms suggest. downstream_timeout needs evidence that the dependency itself is slow or that calls to it timed out. Cite the evidence that identifies the cause (the telltale log line or the metric that changed), not only symptom lines.

Alert: payments-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 15:43 UTC)
Alerting service: payments
Alert time: 2026-05-23T15:43:00Z
Data available from 2026-05-23T14:00:00Z to 2026-05-23T17:00:00Z

Evidence:
Step 1: metrics_query {"aggregation": "mean", "end": "2026-05-23T17:00:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-05-23T14:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check error rate behaviour over time for payments service.)
  Result: M-041: Change detected at 2026-05-23T15:40:00Z: mean 0.38 before, 27.07 after (263.6 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-041] payments.error_rate_pct from 2026-05-23T14:00:00Z to 2026-05-23T16:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.18 max=27.32 mean=12.24 last=26.97; mean=12.24. Change detected at 2026-05-23T15:40:00Z: mean 0.38 before, 27.07 after (263.6 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-23T14:15:00Z = 0.18 (lowest); 2026-05-23T15:40:00Z = 27.07 (first point after the change); 2026-05-23T16:30:00Z = 27.32 (peak); 2026-05-23T16:55:00Z = 26.97 (last).
Step 2: metrics_query {"aggregation": "max", "end": "2026-05-23T17:00:00Z", "metric": "restarts", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-05-23T14:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if payments service restarted around the time of the incident.)
  Result: M-045: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-045] payments.restarts from 2026-05-23T14:00:00Z to 2026-05-23T16:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=0 max=0 mean=0 last=0; max=0. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-05-23T14:00:00Z = 0 (lowest); 2026-05-23T14:00:00Z = 0 (peak); 2026-05-23T16:55:00Z = 0 (last).
Step 3: log_search {"end": "2026-05-23T15:45:00Z", "limit": 30, "query": "deploy,start,error,exception,fail", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-05-23T15:30:00Z"} (asked because: Search logs for any deploys, starts, or errors leading up to the alert.)
  Result: 7 matching log lines.
  [L-0287] 2026-05-23T15:40:05Z payments ERROR write failed: No space left on device (errno=28) path=/var/log/payments/app.log
  [L-0291] 2026-05-23T15:40:37Z payments ERROR WAL archiving failed: could not write file: No space left on device
  [L-0294] 2026-05-23T15:41:04Z payments WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
  [L-0297] 2026-05-23T15:42:07Z payments ERROR request failed status=502 path=/api/v1/orders request_id=req-7f8e0fc2
  [L-0303] 2026-05-23T15:43:02Z payments ERROR request failed status=500 path=/api/v1/orders request_id=req-fb13167e duration_ms=25203
  [L-0305] 2026-05-23T15:43:10Z payments ERROR request failed status=500 path=/api/v1/orders request_id=req-53edd127 duration_ms=2455
  [L-0306] 2026-05-23T15:43:13Z payments ERROR request failed status=500 path=/api/v1/orders request_id=req-552e95fa duration_ms=19859
Step 4: metrics_query {"aggregation": "max", "end": "2026-05-23T17:00:00Z", "metric": "disk_used_pct", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-05-23T14:00:00Z"} (asked because: Confirm disk usage for payments service around the incident time.)
  Result: M-040: Change detected at 2026-05-23T14:40:00Z: mean 42.14 before, 88.72 after (110.5 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-040] payments.disk_used_pct from 2026-05-23T14:00:00Z to 2026-05-23T16:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=41.7 max=100 mean=78.37 last=100; max=100. Change detected at 2026-05-23T14:40:00Z: mean 42.14 before, 88.72 after (110.5 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-23T14:10:00Z = 41.7 (lowest); 2026-05-23T14:40:00Z = 46.86 (first point after the change); 2026-05-23T15:35:00Z = 100 (peak); 2026-05-23T16:55:00Z = 100 (last).
Step 5: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "disk full no space left on device mitigation"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook guidance for handling disk full / out of disk space incidents.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-06-5 (similarity 0.62).
  [R-06-5] Disk full - Mitigation (similarity 0.62): Free space immediately by deleting old rotated logs and stale temporary files, and start log rotation. Then extend the volume. Do not delete database data files by hand. Once stable, trace what grew and put a cleanup or a limit on it.
  [R-06-7] Disk full - Escalation (similarity 0.60): Call the platform team if the volume cannot be extended or the database refuses to restart cleanly after space is freed. Tell the data owner before removing anything that is not plainly a log or temporary file.
  [R-06-4] Disk full - Likely causes (similarity 0.59): Log files with no rotation, a runaway temporary folder, a backup or export that was never cleaned up, or database write-ahead files piling up because shipping them elsewhere has been failing for a while.

Hypotheses from the investigation:
- disk_full: Disk utilization reached 100% and logs explicitly show 'No space left on device' (errno=28) when attempting to write logs and archive WAL files right as the error rate spiked. (evidence: M-041, L-0287, L-0291, M-040)
